$comment: The trust-root ontology. Single source of truth, shared by the deploy script and the SDK.
trustRoot is the correlation key. Adapters with an equal trustRoot are ONE piece of
evidence observed more than once and must saturate, never sum. The 32 adapters below sit
on 19 roots, and the collapse is concentrated where it matters: one passport chip is read
by four of them, five commercial KYC vendors carry eleven more, and the six largest roots
account for 19 of the 32. That is why additive
scoring fails in the adversary's favour — a farm's credentials are maximally correlated,
a real person's are diverse.
forgeCostCents is what it costs an adversary to manufacture the credential.
rentCostCents is what it costs to borrow one from a willing holder. They are separate
because every protocol that hardened did so against sale, and none against rental.
Scoring takes min(forge, rent), so where a class has genuinely solved sale — Idena’s
identity staking, World’s presence check — only the rental figure binds.
Costs are dated human judgements derived from the research in research/, not
measurements. Each carries its source; the derivation of every figure is tabulated in
research/landscape/ontology-coverage.md. Figures as of 2026-07-25.
A cost on an adapter with implemented:false never binds, because no probe can produce
evidence for it. Where such a figure is a placeholder rather than a sourced judgement the
notes say so, and it must be priced from a source before the adapter is implemented.
ageCurve: how weight relates to credential age. 'Decay' = weight falls with age
(liveness, KYC — recency is the signal). 'Ramp' = weight RISES with survival
(vouching registries — a registration that survived challenge windows beats one
minted during last week's reward program). One curve for all classes would hand
full weight to exactly the airdrop-minted cohort.

trustRoots.iris-registry:world-orb: Iris enrolment in World’s Orb registry.
trustRoots.state-document:icao-9303: An ICAO-9303 passport chip signed by a national CSCA. Shared by every ZK-passport tool AND World’s document tier — the single largest correlation cluster in the landscape.
trustRoots.state-registry:aadhaar: A UIDAI-signed Aadhaar payload. Distinct from ICAO-9303: it is a signed file rather than a chip challenge, so possession transfers by copying.
trustRoots.kyc-vendor:persona: A document + selfie check performed by Persona.
trustRoots.kyc-vendor:sumsub: A document + selfie check performed by Sumsub.
trustRoots.kyc-vendor:facetec: FaceTec 3D FaceMap liveness, in any deployment — Synaps-hosted (Anima, Billions), Civic’s direct integration, Holonym’s self-hosted server. Galleries are per-integrator so none of them yields global uniqueness, but a technique that defeats FaceTec defeats all of them, which is what a root is for.
trustRoots.kyc-vendor:fractal: Fractal ID’s own KYC stack, operated centrally and resold to a long list of chains and foundations.
trustRoots.kyc-vendor:unattributed: A document + selfie check by a commercial IDV vendor the credential does not name. Deliberately one root, not several: we cannot rule out that two unattributed checks were performed by the same vendor, and over-correlating costs an honest subject one root while under-correlating pays the adversary. Priced at the floor of the KYC class.
trustRoots.social-vouching:poh: A human vouched on the Proof of Humanity registry.
trustRoots.social-vouching:brightid: A BrightID verification party. Separate from Proof of Humanity: no vendor sits under either, and the two graphs share no members by construction, so counting them independently is sound.
trustRoots.social-trust:circles: A position in the Circles trust graph on Gnosis.
trustRoots.social-account:farcaster: A Farcaster id in the OP-Mainnet IdRegistry, with its rented storage. Account ownership, not personhood — priced at the published storage rent.
trustRoots.social-account:lens: A Lens account on Lens Chain, or the v2 profile NFT on Polygon it migrated from. One root for both registries — migration copied rather than burned, so a subject holding both holds one credential. Account ownership, not personhood: creation is free to the user and gas-sponsored.
trustRoots.ceremony:encointer: Physical attendance at an Encointer key-signing meetup.
trustRoots.biometric-registry:humanode: A 3D face enrolment binding one Humanode validator to one human.
trustRoots.behavioral:wallet-history: A model score over an address’s on-chain history. One root for every such scorer: they read the same public chain state, so two of them are one observation, and the market price of a farmed wallet caps all of them.
trustRoots.aggregate:republished: A protocol that republishes credentials issued elsewhere and adds no evidence of its own. Contributes no cost — whatever it carries is already counted under the root that issued it.

retiredTrustRoots.unknown: Never a root — an admission that the research was not done, which scores as full independence and therefore pays an adversary. Carried by humanity-protocol from revision 12 until revision 34 (Sepolia block 11347272, 2026-07-25), when it was resolved to kyc-vendor:unattributed. Kept here so a score computed as-of a block before that resolves the hash to a name rather than printing it raw.
retiredTrustRoots.kyc-vendor:facetec-synaps: Superseded by the wider kyc-vendor:facetec at revision 34 (Sepolia block 11347272, 2026-07-25). FaceTec's 1:N galleries are per-integrator, so Synaps-hosted deployments really do hold separate databases — but a root prices the adversary's cheapest path, and a technique that defeats FaceTec defeats every deployment of it. Widening merged three roots into one and cost anima-pou and civic-pass their independence from Holonym's biometric check.

adapters.name: World ID (Orb)
adapters.notes: Forging requires defeating iris dedup at an Orb — expensive. Renting does not: an open resale market was documented at $0.50-$15 per verified account (ZachXBT, 2026-04-28). require_user_presence raises the rent floor but does not remove it. Read from WorldIDAddressBook (0x57b930D5…E0330D) and AgentBook on World Chain, both group 1 = Orb. The address book's binding carries a fixed 168-day term, so it hard-expires long before this 1,095-day half-life completes, and the contract refuses a second live binding against the same World ID nullifier — at most one live verified address per human, enforced on chain. The date is the last renewal, not the Orb enrolment, which World keeps off chain; see research/protocols/world-id-onchain-read.md.

adapters.name: World ID (document / NFC)
adapters.notes: Reads the same passport chip as ZKPassport, Self and Rarimo. NOT independent evidence from any of them. There is no permissionless read: a World ID 4.0 credential leaves no per-holder state anywhere on chain — WorldIDVerifier is a view function taking a proof (2 transactions in the proxy's life) and CredentialSchemaIssuerRegistry is keyed by issuer schema id, storing issuer pubkeys and not holders. Both address-keyed World Chain registries (WorldIDAddressBook, AgentBook) consume v3 group-1 proofs, which is the Orb tier only. Reading this tier needs World's Developer Portal with a registered rp_id, which is a vendor on the critical path. Measured 2026-07-25; see research/protocols/world-id-onchain-read.md.

adapters.name: World ID (Selfie Check)
adapters.notes: Liveness only — proves a human was present, never that they are unique or that they hold only one credential. Injection attacks against face liveness rose sharply through 2025, so this decays fast. There is no permissionless read, for the same reason as world-id-document: schema 11 is a v4 credential verified by a stateless view call, and World's own docs scope its Sybil signal per relying party, so even the vendor API answers a question about one RP's user base rather than about the chain. Measured 2026-07-25; see research/protocols/world-id-onchain-read.md.

adapters.name: Proof of Humanity v2
adapters.notes: requiredNumberOfVouches() == 1 and HumanityRevoked has fired once ever. ~1,299 of 1,364 lifetime registrations arrived in four months tracking a $9.94 PNK airdrop 1:1, so the credential is currently airdrop-inflated. Weight by registration age, not the boolean. ageCurve=Ramp: a week-old registration weighs ~0.01, a year-old ~0.5 — the airdrop cohort discounts itself.

adapters.name: Circles v2 (trust graph)
adapters.notes: A sybil costs roughly two days of freely-minted CRC — a cost denominated in the asset the issuer mints is barely a cost. The public indexer carries events named BotCreated and FarmGrown. Valuable only as a graph-position modifier, never as a standalone proof; genuinely independent of every document and biometric root. ageCurve=Ramp for the same reason: the BotCreated cohort is fresh by definition.

adapters.name: Coinbase Verified Account (EAS)
adapters.notes: Persona-rooted per Coinbase's own vendor disclosure. Binds a KYC'd account to an address, one-to-many, with no nullifier. 720,503 issued and 406,022 revoked — always check revocation, never presence alone. Read fully on-chain since 2026-07-25: Coinbase's AttestationIndexer + getAttestation, EASSCAN GraphQL no longer on the critical path.

adapters.name: ZKPassport
adapters.notes: Scopes its nullifier per service and never publishes an unscoped value — good privacy, but it means we cannot detect that this and Self came from one chip. Hence saturation rather than dedup. Verified 2026-07-25 that no permissionless address-keyed read exists: the RootVerifier's verify() is a stateless view (19 logs ever per chain, all admin), and results live in per-integrator contracts under app-scoped nullifiers. See the research file for what would flip this.

adapters.name: Self Protocol
adapters.notes: Read from Celo: five Sourcify-verified integrator registries by eth_call (hub-gated callbacks, no non-proof write path, EIP-712 receiver consent so it cannot be planted), then a bounded client-filtered scan of the hub's DisclosureVerified events, whose recipient is un-indexed. All dates are latest-re-attestation ceilings. Caveats that discount the root's figures: 39% of all 6,212 hub disclosures ever (measured 2026-07-25) are Aadhaar or KYC attestations, not ICAO documents, and the registry path cannot tell which document type minted a positive; the hub is an upgradeable proxy with an unverified implementation; and the global per-document nullifier still means one chip can also feed ZKPassport and World — saturate, never sum. Publishes a global unscoped per-document nullifier on-chain.

adapters.name: Galxe Passport
adapters.notes: Sumsub underneath (Persona in the v2 era); shares its root with Linea PoH. Read passively from the soulbound ERC-721 on BNB Chain (0xE840…3C012, still minting ~2/day as of 2026-07-25) — balanceOf decides held, the owner-keyed _passports storage slot names the token, and issuance is dated exactly by bisecting the contract's monotone mint counter over archive state, with measured anchor bounds as the degraded path. Non-transferability is enforced in code, so held is an act of the subject; burn and Galxe-side revoke both zero the read. The SBT does not disclose document class or credential version — a 'passport' here may be a municipal ID — so passive scoring cannot weight by document strength.

adapters.name: Linea Proof of Humanity V2
adapters.notes: Sumsub-attested via a Verax portal registering no validation modules, so nothing validates a write except the portal's own signature check. Read by enumerating the whole live population from the registry: the 90-day term plus attestedDate being monotone in attestation id confines every unexpired attestation to a ~1,000-id window out of 6.37M, so the probe needs no indexer and no vendor. The hard expiry means this 90-day half-life only ever applies over one credential life, and it leaves 500 live credentials out of 50,475 ever issued — cumulative counts are not population. Linea's own poh-api and PohVerifier still answer true ten months after an attestation expires, so the chain is the stricter source.

adapters.name: Anima Proof of Uniqueness
adapters.notes: Markets uniqueness, delivers liveness: FaceTec's 1:N dedup runs against the integrator's own database, never across customers.

adapters.name: Humanity Protocol (Human ID)
adapters.notes: Root resolved 2026-07-25 from unknown to kyc-vendor:unattributed: their own config defines is_human as “passed a KYC check OR palm enrollment” and the KYC provider is unnamed, so the credential we could actually read is an unattributed document check — which is a root, not an absence of one. Marked not-live: mainnet has been offline since the 2026-06 key compromise, the verification oracle has processed 28 verifications in its entire life and none since 2026-02, and every read requires an OAuth client and a per-verification fee, so there is no permissionless read either. Promote back to live only on a stable relaunch with a published palm_verified population.

adapters.name: Idena
adapters.notes: Marked not-live on scale grounds: 124 validated identities at epoch 214, down from 21,187 at peak. Its sublinear-staking fork killed the puppeteer pools and the network with them. Retained because it is the best-documented failure in the field. Probed anyway since 2026-07-25 — a held identity is reported and scored 0 while live is false, which is the honest shape: checked, found, not counted. Read from restricted.idena.io (the node the official app uses; its API key is a public constant in the deployed bundle — permissionless but protocol-operated, no independent fallback). Decay, not Ramp: identity state expires on a missed validation ceremony, so recency is the whole signal.

adapters.name: BrightID
adapters.notes: Readable, frozen. The one general address->verified surface is the BrightIDSnapshot registry on IDChain (0x81591DC4997A76A870c13D383F8491B288E09344, the contract Snapshot's official strategy reads): 233 unique addresses, first 2022-01-22, last write 2024-06-09, measured over full chain history 2026-07-25. held = a verifier-token signer attested the address met the snapshot app's graph verification; issuedAt = that attestation's timestamp (understates age -> conservative on the Ramp); re-linked addresses read superseded, not unregistered. live:false because the write path needs a BrightID node signature and every node endpoint 502s (probed 2026-07-25) - nobody, honest or adversary, can newly obtain this, so forge/rent are academic and effective cost is zeroed by liveness. IDChain is protocol-operated with a single public RPC: permissionless read, not infrastructure-independent. The prior not-obtainable verdict stands for every other BrightID app: contextIds are app-scoped UUIDs with no on-chain address linkage.

adapters.name: Civic Pass (uniqueness)
adapters.notes: Discontinued 2025-07-31. Root corrected 2026-07-25: FaceTec integrated directly, not Persona — the dedup table names Civic on the FaceTec (direct) row. Retained deliberately: a major competitor still assigns points to Civic stamps for a product that no longer exists, which is exactly the failure the live flag prevents. Now read on-chain from the GatewayToken proxy (0xF65b…F22E, same address on every chain; ERC-3525, gatekeeper network 10 = uniqueness): tokens carry first-class expiry, and the chain confirms the retirement — the latest uniqueness expiry anywhere is 2025-10-27, zero mints since, so every probe honestly answers held:false with the lapse date. An expired biometric dedupe proves a face check happened once, not that the subject is currently unique; the probe refuses to resurrect it, and would notice — without a code change — if Civic ever resumed issuing.

adapters.name: Proof of Humanity v1
adapters.notes: Superseded by v2 but the v1 registry still answers on Ethereum mainnet (0xC5E9dDebb09Cd64DfaCab4011A0D5cEDaf7c9BDb). Shares v2’s root on purpose: a subject registered in both holds one vouched identity, not two, and saturation is what says so. Priced as v2 — the deposit differs, the rental economics do not. Read 2026-07-25: isRegistered is `registered && now - submissionTime <= submissionDuration`, and the struct’s `registered` flag is never cleared on expiry — 33 of 215 sampled submitters have it set with the credential long dead. PoH v2 keeps its own overlay for the frozen contract (ForkModule 0x068a27Db9c3B8595D03be263d52c813cb2C99cCB): 9 registrations are retired there while v1 goes on honouring them, one for 510 days. Term is 730.5 days (was 365.25 until governance changed it), which caps the ramp at 0.75 however long anyone survives. Population enumerated from the chain at block 25,610,404: **2 registered addresses out of 20,740 lifetime submissions**, expiring 2026-09-07 and 2026-11-16. live:true means the contract works, not that it has users.

adapters.name: Rarimo passport registry
adapters.notes: The only project in the family that implements ICAO Active Authentication, which is exactly the clone-resistance the others lack — but AA is optional and PNOAADispatcher auto-passes without it, so the credential cannot be assumed to carry it. Registry lives on Rarimo’s own L2, so reading it means trusting that chain. Same chip as ZKPassport, Self and World’s document tier.

adapters.name: Anon Aadhaar
adapters.notes: Dormant. Its credential is a static, transferable file rather than a challenge to a chip, so “rental” does not even describe the attack — possession transfers by copying, and the holder keeps theirs. Costs are placeholders that never bind while live is false; price them from a source before promoting this entry.

adapters.name: Human Passport (ex-Gitcoin Passport)
adapters.notes: Permissionlessly readable, and now read: GitcoinResolver.getCachedScore(address) on all seven mainnets, no vendor call. The scalar must never be imported at face value: ETHScore#50, a pure wallet-history model, is weighted 16.021, the same as a government ID. So it is rooted at wallet history and priced at the farmed-wallet market ($1–$20 per aged wallet, sybil-incidents table), not at KYC prices. Its high-weight state stamps (Coinbase→Persona, Holonym gov-id, Holonym biometrics, Civic, BrightID, Idena, TrustaLabs) are counted under their own roots; taking the scalar cheaply here is what stops that becoming a double count, and the probe names the restated roots in its detail so the collapse is visible rather than merely safe. Measured on-chain 2026-07-25: maxScoreAge is 7,776,000s (90 days) on every deployment and expiry is enforced, so a passport is a hard-expiring credential and the 180-day half-life only ever applies over the first 90 days of its life.

adapters.name: Human Passport score (EAS attestation)
adapters.notes: The same credential as human-passport, read from the EAS attestation itself (getUserAttestation -> getAttestation) instead of the resolver's cache: adds the attester check, EAS revocation state, and the inline score-v2 stamp list for root decomposition. Shares behavioral:wallet-history with human-passport on purpose - two reads of one credential must saturate, never sum.

adapters.name: Holonym / Human ID (gov-id)
adapters.notes: Four IDV vendors are wired into id-server — Onfido, Sumsub, iDenfy, Veriff — and the credential does not say which one issued it, so its strength is the weakest of the four and its root cannot be attributed. Read permissionlessly from Hub V3 on OP Mainnet (0x2AA822e2…4DfB): sbtOwners for the record, getSBT for the proof's public values, and the issuer in publicValues[4] is checked against Holonym's key because the Hub's own source warns that anyone can mint an SBT under their own issuer. No action-id needs publishing after all — getSBT is keyed on holder and circuit, and the credential reports whichever action it was minted for. Measured on-chain 2026-07-25: the V3.circom constraint expiry - iat < 31,536,001 makes expiry minus one year a proven lower bound on issuance, and the credential hard-expires within a year of the underlying check, so this 730-day half-life only ever applies over that year.

adapters.name: Holonym / Human ID (biometrics)
adapters.notes: Holonym self-hosts FaceTec and does run 1:N /3d-db/search before enrolling, so unlike most of this class the dedup is real — within its own gallery. Against that: id-server mounts an explicit allow-sybils route enrolling into 3d-db groupName 2, described in its own comment as non-sybil-resistant, so a credential of this type may have been issued through a path that deliberately skips dedup and we cannot tell from outside which path produced it — the two paths share one issuer key and one circuit id, so nothing on chain distinguishes them either. Read from the same Hub V3 SBT as holonym-gov-id, under circuit 0x0b512122…3d15 and issuer 0x0d4f849d…d922, dated by the same expiry-minus-one-year bound.

adapters.name: Billions Network (ex-Privado ID)
adapters.notes: A face scan on the Synaps/FaceTec root, so it corroborates Anima and Linea’s biometric tier rather than adding to them. Issuance is centrally controlled by Billions on a chain Billions operates, so the credential being “on-chain” buys no trust — and the population figures are airdrop-inflated.

adapters.name: Fractal ID
adapters.notes: One operator behind KYC for Polygon ID, Ripple/XRPL, Avalanche, Gnosis, Near, Aurora, Acala, Polymath, BNB Chain, Lukso, Aleph Zero, the Arbitrum Foundation and idOS — a root confirmed, unusually, by the operator’s own breach disclosure. PII is stored centrally, which is both the correlation risk and the reason the root is well evidenced. No permissionless per-address read.

adapters.name: zkMe MeID
adapters.notes: A genuine uniqueness claim with a good nullifier design and deployed, readable ZKMEVerifyUpgradeable contracts — but hasApproved(dappAccount, user) is scoped to a registered dapp account, so there is no permissionless “is this address zkMe-verified” read for a party zkMe has not onboarded. Vendor behind the document check is not disclosed.

adapters.name: Sismo
adapters.notes: Dormant — repo activity trails off in 2023 and there is nothing live to consume. Kept because Sismo is the closest existing design to our privacy-composition problem and because its attestations are still referenced by others; its cost is zero by construction, since a republished attestation is already counted under whichever root issued it.

adapters.name: Nomis reputation score
adapters.notes: A multi-chain wallet-history score the user mints as an SBT for a fee. Shares its root with Human Passport and Trusta on purpose: three models reading the same public chain history are one observation, and the farmed-wallet market prices all three.

adapters.name: Trusta.AI Sybil / MEDIA score
adapters.notes: No permissionless read: the score is an API product (1,000 free trial calls, then a Discord conversation), and the company is pivoting to AI-agent scoring. Listed because it is a Human Passport stamp and therefore already inside a score we may read — sharing the wallet-history root is what stops that counting twice.

adapters.name: Farcaster account (IdRegistry)
adapters.notes: Account ownership, never personhood — but permissionlessly readable on OP Mainnet and priced from published on-chain numbers rather than guesses: StorageRegistry.usdUnitPrice() is $0.20/unit/year and TierRegistry.tierInfo(1) is $120/year for Pro, which is the forge figure. Ramp because the aged-account market pays for age, and because two thirds of the registry was minted inside a nine-month subsidy window that ended in 2026-04: at 20 cents and a 730-day half-life an id has to predate that window to clear the negligible-cost floor at all. The registry stores no timestamps, so the probe dates a fid by searching idCounter over archive state; fids <= 193791 were carried in from the predecessor registry by an admin SetIdCounter at block 111904738 and are dated to that import, which understates their age. Farcaster Pro is NOT scored: TierRegistry holds no per-fid subscription state, so a subject's Pro status is derivable only from PurchasedTier logs and no keyless Base endpoint serves those over full history.

adapters.name: Lens account (Lens Chain)
adapters.notes: Account ownership, never personhood, and cheaper than a Farcaster id: creation is gas-sponsored (0.0012 GHO ≈ 0.12¢ to the sponsor, $0 to the user, measured 2026-07-25) with auto-generated usernames minting at ~250/day, so forge is priced at the unsponsored gas path, and rent equals forge: nobody pays more to borrow an account than minting one costs, and the aged-handle premium the resale market charges is a premium on age — which the Ramp curve prices — not on the credential. Ramp for the same reason as farcaster-account: the only thing an adversary cannot mint today is survival — a claimed 2022-era v2 profile — and the probe dates acquisition, not creation, so bought accounts are priced from the sale. Read permissionlessly from Lens Chain ownership-transfer logs (both public RPCs are Lens-operated; permissionless but not infrastructure-independent), with a Polygon LensHub fallback for never-migrated v2 profiles date-bounded at the 2025-04 sunset block. Ownership transfer needs no recipient consent, so the credential can be planted; held must never be read as an act of the subject.

adapters.name: Encointer
adapters.notes: Physical pseudonym parties on a Kusama common-good parachain — the strongest anonymity model in the field and the only one where forging requires a body in a room. Marked not-live on the same grounds as Idena: community-scale, and pivoted to financial inclusion, so the expected number of our subjects holding one is near zero. There is also no EVM read; the credential lives on Substrate accounts. Costs mirror the ceremony class and never bind while live is false. The no-EVM-read claim was verified 2026-07-25 against the full runtime metadata (no EVM binding pallet; accounts are sr25519/blake2 AccountId32, information-theoretically unmappable from an Ethereum address). Watch item: EncointerReputationRings ring proofs are the plausible future EVM export path.

adapters.name: Humanode
adapters.notes: One node, one human, enforced by 3D face liveness at the consensus layer, re-proved every 7 days. Read permissionlessly from the chain's own EVM precompiles: address -> native account (0x..0801, a permanent dual-consent binding that cannot be planted) then isAuthenticated (0x..0800, the consensus layer's own membership test), dated exactly from ActiveAuthentications state (expiry minus the 7-day lifetime, re-verified live every test run). The decay curve is a formality: an active bioauth is never more than 7 days old. Honest population caveat: 82 humans were actively bioauthenticated on 2026-07-25 and zero had claimed an EVM mapping, so no EVM-addressed subject can currently hold this credential; the adapter re-measures that emptiness rather than assuming it. Single Humanode-operated RPC (permissionless, not infrastructure-independent); enrollment trust root is Humanode's robonode + FaceTec, not the chain. Costs remain the face-liveness-class placeholder until priced.
